title: Count the Stretches With a Constant Step

concept.title: A stretch that ends here is a stretch that ended one place earlier, made one longer
body: In a list of numbers, call a stretch of **at least three consecutive numbers** *arithmetic* if the difference between neighbours is the same all the way, such as `3 5 7 9` or `10 7 4`. How many arithmetic stretches does the list contain (stretches in different places are counted separately, even if they overlap)? In `1 2 3 4` there are 3: `1 2 3`, `2 3 4` and `1 2 3 4`.

Let `run(i)` be the number of arithmetic stretches that **end** at the position `i`. If `a[i] - a[i-1]` equals `a[i-1] - a[i-2]`, then every stretch that ended at `i - 1` can be made one number longer, and in addition the new three-number stretch `a[i-2], a[i-1], a[i]` appears: **`run(i) = run(i - 1) + 1`**. Otherwise no stretch can end at `i`: `run(i) = 0`. The answer is the sum of all `run(i)`.

Counting every stretch by itself would be O(n^3) (or O(n^2) with care); the DP gives O(n) time and O(1) memory. A list of 200 000 equal numbers has about 2 * 10^10 stretches, so the answer needs 64 bits. The trick "how many things end here" is the standard way to count subarrays with a property that can only be extended.

statement: A list of `n` numbers is given. Count the stretches of at least three consecutive numbers in which the difference between every two neighbours is the same. Overlapping stretches are all counted.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of values.
outputFormat: Print the number of such stretches.
hints: Let run(i) be the number of such stretches that end at position i.
If the last two differences are equal, run(i) = run(i - 1) + 1; otherwise run(i) = 0.
Add all the run values; use 64-bit numbers.

explanation: run(i), the number of arithmetic stretches that end at i, is run(i - 1) + 1 when the last two differences are equal and 0 otherwise; the answer is the sum of all run values.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

total = 0
run = 0
for i in range(2, n):
    if a[i] - a[i - 1] == a[i - 1] - a[i - 2]:
        run += 1
        total += run
    else:
        run = 0
print(total)
